data.narrative:
Bohr Systems is a pre-seed stage Defense & Security company founded by Rohil Gharat (former Antler, Founders Inc., Cisco) and Samarth Kumbla (Columbia CS '27). The valuation exercise draws on a comp universe of 24 same-sector peers, including 2 public companies (DRSHF, IDEAFORGE.NS) and 8 private firms. Top private comparables include Anduril Industries, Helsing, Shield AI, Saronic, and Quantum-Systems.

The peer-median method is not applicable in this instance. A rigorous narrow-filter approach—isolating pre-seed or adjacent-stage Defense & Security firms with similar valuation tier—yielded fewer than three datapoints, falling short of the minimum threshold for statistical validity. Applying an all-sector median would introduce unacceptable cross-sector distortion. The composition of public and private peers establishes the relevant reference class, but stage-specific density within Defense & Security is insufficient for reliable benchmark triangulation at this time.

Without viable quantitative triangulation methods, a defensible valuation range cannot be derived from the data provided. The key constraint is the absence of same-stage or near-stage comparables in the target sector. Future valuation work should prioritize: (1) tracking seed-stage financings within Defense & Security to build comparable density, and (2) evaluating whether adjacent sectors (aerospace, intelligence) offer methodologically sound cross-sector proxies. Until such data accumulates, valuation remains judgment-driven rather than evidence-based.
